//: The words the story generator speaks with. Every symbol can be extended or replaced by other mods (personality-specific lines are say_<kind>_<personality>). Available names: {char} {item} {reward} {about} {where} {place} {villain} {obstacle} {key} {clue} {feature} {target} {means} {speaker} {hook} {goal} {motive} {topic}.

step_meet_hint: {char.The} in {place} wants a word with you.
Find {char} in {place} and hear what they have to say.
step_deliver_hint_reward: {char.The} in {place} will give you {reward} in exchange for {item}.
Take {item} to {char} in {place}; in return they'll part with {reward}.
step_deliver_hint: Bring {item} to {char} in {place}; it matters to them.
step_info_hint: {char.The} in {place} knows more than they let on. Talk to them.
Find {char} in {place}; they may know something.
step_open_hint: {obstacle.The} bars the way. {key.The} should open it.
step_investigate_hint: Something in {place} may hold answers. Look for {clue.a} and read it.
Search {place} for {clue.a}; read what it says.
step_inspect_hint: Take a close look at {feature} in {place}.
step_confront_hint: It is time to face {char}, in {place}.
step_defeat_hint: {char.The} stands in your way, in {place}. Fight it, or find something that can.
Hunt down {char} in {place} and end it.
step_resolve_hint: Deal with {target}, once and for all.
say_greet_kind: {speaker.The} smiles. "What can I do for you?"
say_greet_nervous: {speaker.The} jumps. "Oh! It's you. Sorry. What is it?"
say_greet_cunning: {speaker.The} gives you a measuring look. "Ah. And what brings you to me?"
say_greet_weary: {speaker.The} sighs. "Another day, another visitor. What is it?"
say_greet_wise: "I wondered when you would come," says {speaker}.
say_meet_gruff: "Listen. {hook} Somebody has to sort it out. {goal}"
say_give: "Take {item}. You'll need it more than I will."
say_give_kind: "I want you to have {item}. Bring it back if you can."
say_give_cunning: "Consider {item} an investment. I'll expect a return, one day."
say_give_nervous: "Take it - take {item}. Just... don't tell anyone where you got it."
say_ask: "I might help you, but first I need {item}. Bring it to me."
say_ask_kind: "I hate to ask, but... could you find {item} for me? It would mean so much."
say_ask_weary: "If you want my help, find me {item}. I'm too tired to go myself."
say_thanks_kind: "Oh, {item}! Bless you. Thank you so much."
say_info: "{about.The}? Last I knew, it was in {where}."
say_confront: {speaker.The} turns to face you. "So. You've come."
say_confront_cold: "You are a nuisance," says {speaker} flatly. "Nothing more."
say_motive: "All I ever wanted was to {motive}. Is that so wrong?"
say_bye: {speaker.The} turns back to what they were doing.
obstacle_locked: {obstacle.The} won't open. It needs something you don't have.
default_story_hook: Nothing in this world happens by accident, and you have a feeling that something here is waiting for you.
default_story_goal: Follow the threads wherever they lead.
default_story_ending: The last thread is tied. Whatever you came here to do, it is done.

strings.lore_empty: You haven't learned anything of note yet.
strings.lore_note_description: A few lines of cramped writing.

feature.name: iron strongbox

appearance.text: A heavy iron strongbox squats here, firmly locked.

feature.description: Riveted iron with a stubborn lock.

locked_strongbox.open_text: {key.The} turns in the lock with a clunk, and the strongbox swings open.

appearance.text: A heavy gate stands unlocked and open.
A heavy gate blocks the way on, locked with a great padlock.

locked_gate.open_text: You unlock the gate with {key}. It swings open with a groan.
locked_gate.locked_text: The gate is padlocked. You need a key.
locked_gate.blocked: A locked gate bars the way.

generic_key.name: #key_adj# key
generic_key.description: A key. Somewhere, there is a lock it fits.
